chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: Pay and show rehearsals at the Grand Terrace
summary: He earned about $44 a week, at most $68, playing three long shows nightly; shows were rehearsed for weeks.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: How much did you get paid in Earl Hine's band?

Oh, nothing hardly. Let me see. In the early '30's, I think I made about $44.00 a week. And the most we got in there was I think -- when we worked in the Grand Terrace was about $68.00 a week. That's the most we ever got and we worked from 10 to 4. And we played three long shows a night, about hour and a half shows. And was all music and was all bang, bang, you know. And then after the show we would play about an hour dance music. All the good arrangements. But they were good arrangements in the show -- all the arrangements.
See, we would -- they would do a show about twice a year, two or three times a year. But for that show, they would rehearse that show for about three months before they'd

do a show. But we would rehearse it about six weeks -- the music for the show before they'd ever put it on. Every day about three or four hours for about six weeks. And when that show went out there, the music, you knew it was good.

You felt good about it because the music was good, the arrangements were good. You knew you were playing them good because we rehearsed them and got them real good, you know. Just like you would rehearse a Broadway show. This is the way we did those shows. And they were good shows. We enjoyed playing them, you know. And they had all good arrangers writing the shows. And Andy Razaf, and what's the guy he wrote -- I forgot his partner's name.
They would write songs for the shows. A lot of good songs they would write. Some of them wouldn't get popular. Some of them would, you know. But they were good shows. They were good songs.
